title: Rahul hits century and Padikkal makes 80 as India close in on New Zealand's 368
dek: The pair added 167 for the second wicket on the third day in Wellington before Kyle Jamieson bowled Padikkal. India were about 300 for two in the final session.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
KL Rahul made a patient century and Devdutt Padikkal 80 as India batted through most of the third day of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Saturday, moving to about 300 for two in reply to the hosts' first-innings 368.

Rahul and Padikkal added 167 for the second wicket before Kyle Jamieson bowled Padikkal early in the final session, ending what one report called a stand built "against the run of play" for New Zealand's bowlers. Reports at that point gave India's score as between 295 and 305 for two, leaving them roughly 65 to 75 runs behind with eight wickets in hand. Play was continuing when this report was filed.

## The day's play

India resumed on 159 for one, with Rahul on 52 and Padikkal in the teens, after Yashasvi Jaiswal's 85 had given them a quick start on Friday. On a pitch that offered the New Zealand seamers little, the pair added 80 runs in 27 overs in the morning session to reach 239 for one at lunch, with Rahul on 93 off 197 balls and Padikkal on 53 off 118, according to reports.

Rahul completed his hundred soon after the break, off 207 balls according to one report, giving him Test centuries in all four of the SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia), a rare feat for an Asian batter, the report said. India reached tea at 277 for one, with Rahul on 107 and Padikkal on 71, and trailing by 91.

Padikkal looked set for his first Test century before Jamieson broke through. He faced 175 balls.

Matt Henry, who removed Jaiswal on Friday, was New Zealand's most economical bowler. At lunch Henry had one for 52 from 19 overs, seven of them maidens, while Jacob Duffy had conceded 89 runs from 15 overs, according to reports.

## Earlier in the match

New Zealand, put in after India won the toss, recovered from 70 for five thanks to a 216-run sixth-wicket stand between Henry Nicholls, who carried his bat for 175, and Glenn Phillips, who made 118. Jasprit Bumrah took four for 92 and Akash Deep three for 53.

## What's at stake

This is the first of two Tests, with the second in Christchurch, and the series counts towards the World Test Championship, in which New Zealand lead the table and India are fourth. A substantial first-innings lead on Sunday would give India's bowlers two days to try to force a win.

Play on day four begins at 3:30 am IST on Sunday. A full report on the day's play will follow in the next edition.
